sections.body: Picture station signage, waiting halls, taxis outside, luggage, platforms, and travelers heading north or south.

sections.title: Why it belongs
sections.body: It helps travelers handle intercity movement without confusing the train station with bus terminals.

sections.title: Travel moment
sections.body: Use it when catching a train, arriving by rail, or arranging a pickup from the station.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Arrive with time for tickets, bags, and platform finding, especially if it is your first Vietnamese train.

entries.summary: Mien Dong Bus Station is an important intercity bus-terminal name for eastern and northern routes, where exact address and pickup details can matter a lot.
entries.context: Bến xe Miền Đông names the bus station, but travelers should watch for old and new location confusion.
entries.tip: Confirm the terminal address with your bus operator before leaving, especially for early departures.
entries.rationale: It belongs because bus travel in Vietnam depends on knowing the correct terminal, not just the city.

sections.title: About
sections.body: A major intercity bus station name in HCMC, associated with many routes out of the city.

sections.title: Hear the name
sections.body: Bến xe Miền Đông means Eastern Bus Station, a key phrase for bus tickets and taxi rides.

sections.title: What to picture
sections.body: Picture coaches, ticket counters, luggage, waiting areas, drivers calling routes, and busy terminal roads.

sections.title: Why it belongs
sections.body: It gives travelers the terminal vocabulary needed for practical intercity movement from Saigon.

sections.title: Travel moment
sections.body: Use it when booking buses, confirming pickup, or telling a driver which terminal you need.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Because locations can be confusing, verify the exact address and operator instructions before travel.

entries.summary: Mien Tay Bus Station is the practical western bus-terminal name for many Mekong Delta and westbound trips, useful for tickets, taxis, and early departures.
entries.context: Bến xe Miền Tây means Western Bus Station and helps distinguish it from Mien Dong.
entries.tip: If your trip points toward the Mekong Delta, check whether this is the correct terminal before booking transport.
entries.rationale: It belongs because first-time travelers often connect HCMC with Delta routes by bus.

sections.title: About
sections.body: A major western bus terminal in HCMC, commonly associated with routes toward the Mekong Delta.

sections.title: Hear the name
sections.body: Bến xe Miền Tây means Western Bus Station, a practical phrase for terminal directions.

sections.title: What to picture
sections.body: Picture coaches, route boards, luggage, ticket counters, food stalls, and travelers heading west.

sections.title: Why it belongs
sections.body: It helps travelers name the right transport hub for trips beyond Saigon, especially westbound routes.

sections.title: Travel moment
sections.body: Use it when booking a Delta bus, arranging a taxi to the terminal, or meeting a bus operator.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Terminal names sound similar at first, so distinguish Miền Tây from Miền Đông carefully.

entries.summary: Bach Dang Waterbus Station gives travelers the specific pier name for river boarding, clearer than the broader wharf when timing, tickets, and platforms matter.
entries.context: Bến tàu thủy Bạch Đằng points to the waterbus or river-boarding pier at the Bach Dang area.
entries.tip: Use this when boarding, and use Bach Dang Wharf when you only mean the riverfront area.
entries.rationale: It belongs because river experiences need exact boarding language, not just scenic waterfront names.

sections.title: About
sections.body: A specific river pier at Bach Dang used for waterbus or boat-boarding plans.

sections.title: Hear the name
sections.body: Bến tàu thủy Bạch Đằng means Bach Dang water pier, useful for boarding directions.

sections.title: What to picture
sections.body: Picture a pier on the Saigon River, boats arriving, ticket checks, skyline views, and people waiting.

sections.title: Why it belongs
sections.body: It separates the practical boarding point from the more general Bach Dang waterfront area.

sections.title: Travel moment
sections.body: Use it when catching a waterbus, meeting for a boat ride, or confirming where boarding happens.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Arrive with enough time to find the correct pier, especially if the wharf area is busy.

entries.summary: Ben Thanh Metro Station is the central station name beside the famous market, useful for meeting, orientation, and rail navigation without making schedule promises.
entries.context: Ga Bến Thành names the station, while Chợ Bến Thành names the market nearby.
entries.tip: Keep station entrances and market entrances separate in your plan, especially when meeting someone.
entries.rationale: It belongs because Ben Thanh is becoming both a market landmark and a rail-navigation point.

sections.title: About
sections.body: A central metro station name associated with Ben Thanh Market and downtown Saigon orientation.

sections.title: Hear the name
sections.body: Ga Bến Thành means Ben Thanh Station, distinct from Chợ Bến Thành, the market.

sections.title: What to picture
sections.body: Picture a modern station entrance near central streets, market traffic, signs, and people meeting nearby.

sections.title: Why it belongs
sections.body: It helps travelers understand Ben Thanh as a transport reference as well as a market landmark.

sections.title: Travel moment
sections.body: Use it when meeting near the station, reading transit directions, or orienting around Ben Thanh.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Station details can change, so confirm current entrances and service before relying on it for timing.
